waves.title: Commercial cleaning rates per hour: the 2026 numbers
waves.keywords: commercial cleaning rates per hour uk, office cleaning cost per hour, how to price a cleaning contract, contract cleaning rate card, cleaning charge out rate
waves.brief:
Reader: the owner of a contract cleaning firm, £200k to £5m turnover, putting one number on a multi-site office quote, and the FM manager deciding whether a £16 an hour bid is a bargain or a firm that will fail mid-contract. Fifty pence wrong across 400 hours a week is the year's profit.

What ranks now: contractors' own marketing. Clean360's 2026 pricing guide, Soluxe on London offices, Checkatrade and Fantastic Services guides written for householders, MyJobQuote, Airtasker (£8 to £15, below the legal floor) and Whito, an agency selling to cleaning firms. Every result sells cleaning or sells to cleaners, and none builds the rate up from cost.

Structure, in commitment order: the legal floor built line by line to cost per productive hour; overhead and margin on top; what the market bears, with vendor ranges attributed as vendor claims; the four things that move a rate (nights and weekends, travel between sites, consumables in or out, TUPE inheritance); a worked 400 hour a week contract; the three ways firms underprice.

SOURCE ANCHORS, checked 17 November 2026, each attributed in the same sentence as the figure. National Living Wage is £12.71 for 21 and over from 1 April 2026 (GOV.UK release, 1 April 2026), rising to £13.21 from 1 April 2027 (GOV.UK, 28 October 2026). Employer Class 1 NIC is 15% above a £5,000 secondary threshold, Employment Allowance £10,500 (HMRC 2026/27: confirm on GOV.UK, state the date checked). The real Living Wage, written into many buyer specifications, is £14.10 outside London and £15.45 in London, announced 15 October 2026 (Living Wage Foundation). Published rates disagree and the piece must say why: Whito's September 2026 review gives £15 to £25 per cleaner hour (£21.50 to £25.50 London), Clean360 £18 to £35, Soluxe £20 to £35 London. None states whether consumables, management, equipment or holiday cover are included, and every publisher of a range is a seller. Do not assert a trade body average unless the writer sources and dates one.

STRUCTURAL: 'commercial cleaning rates per hour' in the first paragraph. The cost build-up (wage, employer NIC, holiday, pension, cover, equipment, consumables, management, overhead, margin, charge-out rate) must be a table with an April 2026 and an April 2027 column. Link out to GOV.UK minimum wage rates, GOV.UK employer NIC rates and the Living Wage Foundation rates page.

OUT OF SCOPE: cleaning technique, products, dilution. Hard FM is out: no plant, HVAC or factory maintenance rates.

waves.title: How to win a public sector cleaning tender in 2027
waves.keywords: public sector cleaning tender, how to win a cleaning contract council, crown commercial service cleaning framework, social value weighting cleaning bid, find a tender cleaning contracts
waves.brief:
Reader: the owner or bid lead of a cleaning, window cleaning, washroom or grounds firm with private contracts already, deciding whether to spend four weeks and real money chasing public work.

What ranks now: bid-writing consultancies and tender-alert subscriptions, Hudson Succeed, Executive Compass, Tracker and Stotles, plus council procurement pages that give the rules and none of the economics. Each sells a retainer or a subscription, so each says public work is winnable and none says when it is not.

Structure, in commitment order: where the work is advertised and the registration you cannot bid without; which lot you are eligible for; the pass or fail gates that kill small bidders (insurance levels, filed accounts, accreditations, comparable contracts); how the score is built, with social value scored rather than box-ticked; the cost of a bid against contract value, and the walk-away test; TUPE, which turns a win into a loss.

SOURCE ANCHORS, checked 17 November 2026, each attributed in the same sentence as the figure. The Procurement Act 2023 came into force on 24 February 2025 and notices and supplier information now sit on the Central Digital Platform, an expanded Find a Tender Service (Cabinet Office guidance). From 1 April 2026 suppliers awarded a below-threshold contract must register there and obtain a unique identifier (same guidance, paragraph 74). PPN 002 requires in-scope organisations to apply a minimum 10% weighting, or an equivalent measurement, of the total score for social value, for procurements commenced under the Act on or after 1 October 2025 (GOV.UK, PPN 002). It binds central government only, so say plainly that councils and NHS trusts set their own weighting. Crown Commercial Service became the Government Commercial Agency on 1 April 2026, and its agreement RM6232, Facilities Management and Workplace Services, runs 9 June 2022 to 8 March 2027, Soft FM split by annual value: lot 3a up to £1m, 10 suppliers; 3b £1m to £7m, 17 suppliers; 3c over £7m, 10 suppliers (GCA agreement pages). That expiry is the hook. Nobody publishes a credible cleaning bid win rate and consultancy success rates are self-reported, so say so rather than quote one.

STRUCTURAL: 'public sector cleaning tender' in the first paragraph. The RM6232 Soft FM lots, supplier counts and the 8 March 2027 expiry must be a table. Link out to Find a Tender, GOV.UK PPN 002 and the GCA RM6232 page.

OUT OF SCOPE: hard FM lots, maintenance, HVAC and engineering bids.

waves.title: What the April 2027 wage rise does to your margin
waves.keywords: national living wage april 2027 cleaning contracts, 13.21 national living wage, employer national insurance cleaning business, cleaning contract price increase letter, labour cost increase facilities management
waves.brief:
Reader: the owner or FD of a labour-heavy service firm, cleaning, guarding, grounds or washroom, with fixed-price contracts running through April 2027, deciding whether to go back to clients for an uplift, absorb it, or let the contract lapse. Also the FM manager receiving those letters. A January notice is the last practical point before April.

What ranks now: payroll and accountancy pages, Xero, IRIS, Moorepay, Peninsula and CIPP, plus law firm Budget summaries. All state the rates correctly. None converts the change into pence per charged hour on a cleaning contract, then into a percentage uplift to ask for.

Structure, in commitment order: what changes and when; true cost per hour of an NLW cleaner before and after, built from wage, employer NIC, holiday, pension and cover; the uplift that holds margin flat, with the point that a 3.9% wage rise is not a 3.9% price rise; differentials, since the 18 to 20 rate rises faster and supervisors a pound above the floor get compressed; what to send a client, and what an indexation clause should say.

SOURCE ANCHORS, checked 17 November 2026, each attributed in the same sentence as the figure. From 1 April 2027 every rate rises 3.9% (GOV.UK release, 28 October 2026): 21 and over to £13.21 from £12.71, 18 to 20 to £11.27 from £10.85, and 16 to 17 and apprentices to £8.31 from £8.00, the April 2026 figures coming from GOV.UK's 1 April 2026 release. They apply from the first full pay reference period beginning on or after 1 April 2027. The Low Pay Commission's October 2026 letter says the rise falls short of its own estimate of two thirds of median earnings, against a consultation range of £13.02 to £13.34. Employer Class 1 NIC stays at 15% with the secondary threshold frozen at £5,000 and Employment Allowance at £10,500 (Autumn Budget, 28 October 2026, per employer summaries). Those summaries disagree on 2027/28 thresholds, so confirm them on the GOV.UK employer NIC page, state the date checked, and assert nothing beyond it. The real Living Wage is £14.10 outside London and £15.45 in London, announced 15 October 2026 and due by 1 May 2027 (Living Wage Foundation): on those contracts the statutory rise is not the binding number.

STRUCTURAL: 'National Living Wage' and £13.21 both in the first paragraph. One table of rates showing April 2026, April 2027, pence and percentage. A second table of cost per hour before and after for one cleaner, ending in the uplift needed. Link out to GOV.UK minimum wage rates, the LPC recommendations release and GOV.UK employer NIC.

OUT OF SCOPE: hard FM trades and engineer pay.

waves.title: What a cleaning business is actually worth in 2026
waves.keywords: cleaning business valuation uk, sell a cleaning business, cleaning company ebitda multiple, how much is my cleaning company worth, facilities management acquisition uk
waves.brief:
Reader: the owner of a cleaning, window cleaning, pest control or guarding firm, typically 55 to 70, £1m to £15m turnover, deciding whether to sell, hold, or spend two years fixing the business first. Also the bolt-on buyer. The immediate decision is whether to take a broker's call.

What ranks now: brokers and advisers, exclusively. CT Acquisitions, Clearly Acquired, KBS Corporate, Eilla, Aviaan and US valuation calculators. Every page offers a free valuation and a range, and most are American: CT Acquisitions quotes 4x to 6x EBITDA for firms with $500k to $2m EBITDA, in dollars, to UK readers. No independent UK publisher explains what a buyer actually prices in soft FM, which is contract tenure, labour dependency and customer concentration.

Structure, in commitment order: the two numbers a buyer starts from, adjusted EBITDA and recurring contracted revenue; why soft FM is priced below hard FM; the five discounts, customer concentration, short or rolling terms, owner dependency, TUPE liabilities and unpriced wage exposure on fixed-price work; who is buying now; the pre-sale fixes worth doing; deal structure, because an earnout is not the headline price.

SOURCE ANCHORS, checked 17 November 2026, from filed accounts rather than broker ranges, each attributed in the same sentence as the figure. OCS Group Topco Limited's consolidated accounts for the year ended 31 December 2025 report revenue of £2,658.6m against £2,222.8m, growth of 19.6% with organic growth of 5.5%, adjusted EBITDA up 34.3% to £191.6m from £142.7m, margin widening to 7.2% from 6.4%, and gross profit at 14.2% of revenue against 13.5%: the real margins of soft FM at scale, and the sanity check on any multiple. The same accounts show acquisition spend of £105.3m against £157.8m, and that on 1 July 2025 OCS acquired 100% of Greig Avinou, a window cleaning, exterior maintenance and platform hire provider, with consideration in note 14 to be pulled from the filing and cited. Multiples disagree and the piece must say why: Cooper Parry's December 2025 UK FM deals pack reportedly puts FM near 6.4x with a 25% private company discount and soft FM at the low end, and the writer must open that PDF and verify both figures or leave them out; CT Acquisitions' 4x to 6x is US dollars; Clearly Acquired gives 3.5x to 7.0x. None separates soft from hard FM, or contracted from ad hoc revenue. Do not blend them into one number.

STRUCTURAL: 'cleaning business valuation' in the first paragraph. A table of discounts and premiums with direction and rough size, flagged as indicative not sourced. Link out to Companies House filing history for OCS Group Topco Limited; link internally to this wave's margin piece.

OUT OF SCOPE: hard FM and M and E contractors.
